title: The AI Guard guard for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents: the four legs you call, the tool wrapper, and what each leg sends

prose.text: The AgentCore integration is a guard object that an agent's own loop calls; AgentCore Runtime hosts the code but offers no interception point. {{guard-not-hook}} {{blocked-raises}}

guard-not-hook.statement: The integration is a guard the agent's own loop calls at four legs (scan the prompt before the model, the response after it, a tool's input before it runs, its output before it re-enters the model); nothing is automatic beyond tools wrapped with `guard_tool`.

quotes: before-model   scan the prompt going to the model
after-model    scan the model's response
before-tool    scan a tool call's input
after-tool     scan a tool call's output
**You place the calls.** Unlike the SDK hooks, nothing is automatic beyond the tools you wrap with `guard_tool`. A leg you do not call is a leg not scanned.

blocked-raises.statement: Each `scan_*` method returns the verdict on allow and raises `AIGuardBlocked`, carrying the leg, the verdict and the transaction ID, on a block; under the default postures a scan error or unscannable content raises it too.

quotes: Every `scan_*` method returns the verdict dict on allow and raises `AIGuardBlocked` (carrying `leg`, `verdict`, `transaction_id`) on block.

Missing credentials, an unreachable or erroring AI Guard API, a scan that exceeds its `timeout`, and a verdict without an `action` all block unless you choose `on_error="allow"`.

guard-tool-shapes.statement: `guard_tool` scans a tool's input before it runs and its output before returning, binding arguments to parameter names and dropping a `self` or `cls` receiver; an async tool is awaited and its scans run in a worker thread, and a generator or async-generator tool is drained so its whole output is scanned once before the first item is yielded.

quotes: An `async def` tool is wrapped by an `async def` wrapper that awaits the tool before scanning its output -- and runs the scan itself in a worker thread
A generator or async-generator tool is wrapped by a generator of the same kind that drains the tool and scans the whole output before yielding the first item.
`guard_tool()` binds a tool's arguments to their parameter names before scanning

streaming-caller.statement: Non-streamed model calls are covered; for a streamed response the guard intercepts nothing, and the agent code chooses whether to scan each buffered chunk or the assembled text.

quotes: **Streaming.** For a streamed model response you choose when to scan (per buffered chunk or on the assembled text); the guard does not intercept the stream for you.
Non-streamed model calls are fully covered

source-code-detector.statement: The README reports that on a profile with the source-code detector enabled, tool input, which is a serialized JSON object, can be flagged on its own (arguments as plain as `{"x": "x"}`), so the input leg blocks before the tool runs and a benign tool call is denied; it advises a profile without that detector for tool legs, or scanning tool output only.

quotes: `tool_event.input` is a serialized JSON object by construction, and on a profile with the source-code detector enabled that shape can be flagged on its own merits -- a tool called with arguments as ordinary as `{"x": "x"}` is enough.
use a profile without that detector for the tool legs, or scan tool output only.
The input leg then blocks before the tool runs, so the output leg never happens and a benign tool call is denied.

latency.statement: Each leg adds one scan and each tool round two; `timeout=` bounds the connect and, separately, the response read, so a peer trickling bytes costs at most about twice the timeout.

quotes: Each leg adds one scan call; a tool round adds two (input + output).
a peer that trickles bytes costs at most about twice `timeout` rather than stalling the caller indefinitely
`timeout=` bounds the connect and, separately, the response read

tool-event-shape.summary: Whether the AgentCore and Strands tool legs reach AI Guard as a structured tool event that gets a tool-specific verdict.

positions.says: The AgentCore README says the tool input is sent as a tool_event, which lets AI Guard return a tool-specific verdict such as context poisoning or credential leakage instead of treating the result as plain text.

quotes: it is the only seat positioned to treat a tool call as a `tool_event`, which is what lets AI Guard return a tool-specific verdict (`context poisoning`, `credential leakage`) instead of seeing the tool result merely as text in the next prompt.

positions.says: The Strands README says the same of its tool-output leg.

quotes: a tool result is scanned as a `tool_event`, so AI Guard returns a tool-specific verdict (`context poisoning`, `credential leakage`) instead of seeing it as plain text.

positions.says: Both modules serialize the tool event into the single content string, noting that AI Guard scans one string per call, and their notes also say the API rejects any tool ecosystem but mcp with HTTP 400, a check that would need a structured field.

quotes: {"response": ...} or {"tool_event": {...}}. AI Guard scans a single string
# The scan API accepts exactly one tool ecosystem today: "mcp". Every other

tool-event-shape.impact: What AI Guard receives at the pin is text in content (tool-event-serialized); whether it recognizes that text as a tool event and returns tool-specific detections is not shown by the code, the SDK or Help. The modules' log code reads a tool_detected field that their verdict parser never fills.
